issues.description: ClassPathResourceHandler is not patched, unlike the official fix (DirectoryTraversal.protectAgainstInClassPath). Classpath static-file traversal remains unmitigated; if classpath serving is used, that sibling sink is still exposed.
regressions_ran=0 and pov_before_reproduced=false, so both the fix's effectiveness and absence of regressions rest on code reasoning and the added unit test rather than executed evidence.
Minor TOCTOU: containment is verified on the canonical path at getResource time, but the file is opened later by the caller; acceptable and equivalent to the official design.

result.root_cause: Resolved static-file resources were returned without verifying the canonicalized target stays within the configured base directory, letting traversal sequences escape to arbitrary files.
result.summary: Our patch adds a canonicalize-then-verify-containment check to ExternalResourceHandler.getResource(), which is the CWE-022 defense-of-record and actually more robust than the official startsWith(folder) string comparison for the external static-file vector that is the CVE's sink. It fails closed and preserves legitimate in-base access. The main shortfall versus ground truth is completeness: the official fix also hardened ClassPathResourceHandler, which our patch leaves untouched, so classpath traversal is not covered. Runtime evidence is thin (POV never reproduced, 0 regressions run), but the mechanism is sound for the targeted external sink.
